# FDG8011

> AVOID overloading custom attribute constructors.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.2 Attributes.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8011
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Give the attribute '{0}' a single constructor

FDG8011 reports a non-abstract attribute class, a class derived from System.Attribute, that declares more than one constructor that is neither private, protected nor private protected, the constructors that an attribute application can call. Removing a constructor changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Having only one constructor clearly communicates to the user which arguments are required and which are optional.
